summary.text:
We need answer with single fenced ST block containing ENGINEERING_CONTRACT comment, CONTRACT_RULES JSON comment, and implementation. Need parse requirements. Need implement function block with interface as provided. Need decide semantics.

Let's restate task.

Inputs:
estop BOOL FALSE emergency triggered, TRUE no emergency.
opeMode FALSE manual, TRUE auto.
valveAStart etc buttons.
autoStart button.
processMode BOOL.
levelSensor INT cm.
mixMotorComplete BOOL.
Outputs valves A-D run, mixMotorRun.

Requirements:
Emergency stop: when estop=FALSE, all equipment stops immediately. This likely overrides everything. Outputs FALSE. Need ensure no edge triggers cause later? On each scan if estop false, all outputs false. Also state reset? probably auto sequence stops/reset maybe.

Manual Mode opeMode=false: manually control start/stop of valves A,B,C,D, and mixing motor. Example pressing valve A start button rising edge toggles valve A. It says pressing button again toggles off. So separate start buttons for each valve/motor toggle with rising edge. These outputs should work only in manual and no estop. Need R_TRIG per input for toggle. Manual outputs should not be affected by auto. If estop false, low. If opeMode false and estop true, manual toggle controls outputs. Need remember outputs latch? Since PLC output computed each scan, if input not edge, output hold previous state. Need internal booleans for manual states, because outputs can be overridden in auto? We need manage modes. We can maintain manual state variables per equipment, toggled on edges in manual. Outputs in manual equal these states. In auto, separate auto state.

Auto mode opeMode=true: equipment operates automatically. Press autoStart button to start automatic process. Is edge or level? "Press the autoStart button to start" likely rising edge. Need start sequence. Once start, first opening valve A. Then based on levelSensor reaches 50 cm close A open B. Then reaches 80 close B. Based on processMode:
- if processMode=false: start mixing motor; after receiving mixing complete signal, stop motor, open valve D, and automatic process ends.
- if processMode=true: open valve C; when levelSensor reaches 100, close C, start motor; after mixing complete signal, stop motor, open valve D, and automatic process ends.

Need consider automatic process completion retains valveD open? "open valve D, and automatic process ends." Does valve D stay open after process ends? likely yes until maybe autoStart again? In auto process ends, outputs? Need interpret. In automatic mode, process ends after opening D, maybe valveD remains TRUE? Requirement says open valve D, process ends. It doesn't say close D. So retain valveD run true and motor false after complete. Other valves closed. Starting a new auto process with autoStart should reset and reopen A, close D? It says first opening valve A. It implies automatic process from initial state where other valves off. We need when autoStart edge occurs, clear previous auto states and turn valve A true. Should valve D be closed when starting new process? "Press autoStart button to start automatic process, first opening valve A." It doesn't explicitly say close D. But process flow begins opening A; likely any previously open D should close. Need reset all auto outputs at start to specific initial: valveA true; others false. Yes.

Need define state machine stages. Need use scan logic. Potential issue level conditions "reaches 50" and "reaches 80" use >=? Sensor cm. reaches 50 likely levelSensor >=50. But strict? "reaches" normally at least. But need avoid skip if sensor jumps? Use >=. For 80 similarly. For 100 similarly. But if processMode false, no 100. Need ensure stage transitions on levels only after prior stage active and estop true? In auto.

Need implement auto mode states. Use internal enum or INT state. Could use CASE state. Need handle estop reset.

Need carefully handle manual/auto interaction. Mode switching: If opeMode changes, what happens to outputs? Requirements separate. In manual outputs are manual latches; in auto outputs are auto sequence. If mode switches, we likely switch outputs to respective mode. Manual toggles retained? The buttons only toggles in manual. Do manual states reset upon entering auto? Probably not needed; outputs auto override. Entering manual after auto, manual outputs from last manual state (unless estop). But could be undefined initial false. Fine.

Need handle estop: all outputs false regardless mode. When estop returns true? Do outputs resume? For manual latches, if estop was triggered, "all equipment stops immediately". When estop cleared, should equipment remain stopped until operator restarts? Usually estop latches stop; when reset, equipment won't automatically restart. For manual toggles, estop should force outputs false, but internal manual state? If internal toggles remain true, when estop clears outputs would resume, which may be unsafe. Need decide. Emergency stop likely should reset all start states so operators must restart manually. Automatic sequence should also stop and reset; after estop clear, needs autoStart again. So implement: when estop false, set all manual states false, auto sequence state idle, and outputs false. On clearing estop, all remain off. This matches safety. Need ensure not latching estop? "when emergency stop signal is triggered" immediate stop. "estop=FALSE signal triggered" no explicit reset procedure. likely direct low signal. But should reset internals on estop while low. Could also be level-triggered low; if low, continuous reset. When goes high, idle.

Need autoStart edge. Should only start in auto mode and estop true? Requirement auto mode process starts by autoStart. We should ensure if autoStart pressed while manual mode and then switching? Not relevant. Use R_TRIG on autoStart. If opeMode true and estop true and rising edge, start sequence. What if process already running and autoStart pressed? Could restart from initial. Reasonable.

Need manage mixMotorComplete. In automation, after start mixing motor, wait for mixMotorComplete signal. It may be level or edge? "after receiving the mixing complete signal" likely when input TRUE. Need use level not edge? If mixMotorComplete is momentary, edge should detect. Usually complete signal pulses; use R_TRIG to avoid state stuck if remains true? But "receiving signal" could be rising edge. Need use R_TRIG for complete. However if complete signal already true when motor starts, should not immediately stop? It should wait for completion after mixing. Therefore rising edge after motor start. A level true at start could falsely complete. Use R_TRIG with auto sequence state mixing. But if signal pulses before state? Not. Use edge.

Need R_TRIG instances. Need both manual buttons and autoStart, mixMotorComplete. Could use R_TRIG declarations.

Need outputs assignment.

Potential issue CODESYS R_TRIG requires VAR instance. Use local R_TRIG for each button and complete and autoStart. Each has CLK input and Q output. We'll call rtrig(CLK:=input); then IF rtrig.Q.

Need decide internal auto state enum. Could define TYPE within ST block? Need within same fenced ST block can include TYPE. We can define:

TYPE AUTO_STATE : (IDLE, VALVE_A, VALVE_B, WAIT_B_80, MIXING, VALVE_C, WAIT_C_100, MIXING_C, COMPLETE, DONE) END_TYPE;

But state transitions differ:
ProcessMode false:
IDLE -> after start: VALVE_A (open A)
Wait level >=50 -> close A, open B, state VALVE_B
Wait level >=80 -> close B, start motor, state MIXING
Wait mixMotorComplete edge -> stop motor, open D, process ends -> DONE (or COMPLETE)
ProcessMode true:
IDLE -> VALVE_A
level >=50 -> close A open B -> VALVE_B
level >=80 -> close B, open C -> VALVE_C (note not start motor yet)
Wait level >=100 -> close C, start motor -> MIXING_C
Wait complete edge -> stop motor, open D -> DONE.

Could simplify with stages:
AUTO_WAIT_A: valveA true
AUTO_WAIT_B: valveB true
AUTO_WAIT_C: valveC true
AUTO_MIXING: motor true
AUTO_DONE: valveD true
No need separate B_80; after level >=80, branch processMode. For processMode false, from AUTO_WAIT_B directly to MIXING. For processMode true, from AUTO_WAIT_B to WAIT_C. Good.

Use enum:
TYPE AUTO_STATE : (IDLE, OPEN_A, OPEN_B, WAIT_C, MIXING, DONE);
END_TYPE

But processMode true and false share MIXING. Need complete transition in MIXING to DONE. Okay. In MIXING, motor true. On completion -> motor false, D open -> DONE. For processMode false: OPEN_B -> when level>=80 -> close B, start motor, state MIXING. For true: OPEN_B -> when level>=80 -> close B, open C, state WAIT_C. Wait C -> when level>=100 -> close C, start motor, state MIXING.
DONE holds valve D true. "process ends". Could maybe state DONE with valve D true and stay. If autoStart new, from DONE to OPEN_A closing D.

What about autoStart if DONE? It restarts.

Need handle level thresholds before state? Example level sensor may already >50 when start? Process begins opening A. It should wait until level reaches 50; if already above? Industrial: valve A open fills tank; if level already high maybe shouldn't start? But requirement says press start opening valve A, when level sensor reaches 50 close A. If sensor >50 due previous? Could close immediately. Fine.

Need ensure outputs set based on state at end. If estop false, state IDLE; outputs false. Should state be set IDLE when estop low. If estop false, auto state forced IDLE; on estop true remains IDLE. Good.

Need separate manual internal states. Use BOOL internal:
manualValveA, manualValveB, manualValveC, manualValveD, manualMixMotor. Toggle on rising edge in manual mode and estop true? Should manual toggles be allowed only if estop true. If estop false, no toggle and reset internal states. We'll implement.

Important: Manual mode inputs valveBStart, C, D, mixMotorStart. Need toggle each.

Outputs:
valveARun := (NOT opeMode AND estop AND manualValveA?) Or autoModeOutput? Need combine based opeMode. But in manual, if estop true, outputs from manual states. In auto, outputs from auto state. We can produce autoValveARun etc based on state. At end:
IF NOT estop THEN all false; 
ELSIF NOT opeMode THEN
 valveARun := manualValveA;
 valveBRun := manualValveB;
 valveCRun := manualValveC;
 valveDRun := manualValveD;
 mixMotorRun := manualMixMotor;
ELSE
 valveARun := autoValveA;
 valveBRun := autoValveB;
 valveCRun := autoValveC;
 valveDRun := autoValveD;
 mixMotorRun := autoMixMotor;
END_IF

Need define auto outputs in each scan based on state. Could have local auto flags. Use state variable autoState. At each scan, compute local_autoValveA etc false initially, set according to state. But state transitions depend level and processMode and complete edge. Need use state from previous scan; compute transitions before setting outputs.

Potential issue same-scan: we compute autoState transitions based on current input and previous state. Then compute outputs from new autoState. Good.

Need use R_TRIG for buttons. R_TRIG evaluates CLK current and stores previous. If call R_TRIG for inputs in code every scan. Need call all R_TRIGs before logic.

Pseudo:

FUNCTION_BLOCK MaterialProportioningProcess
VAR_INPUT ... END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT ... END_VAR
VAR
  manualValveA : BOOL := FALSE;
  ...
  autoState : AUTO_STATE := AUTO_STATE#IDLE;
  rt_valveA : R_TRIG;
  rt_valveB : R_TRIG;
  rt_valveC : R_TRIG;
  rt_valveD : R_TRIG;
  rt_mixMotor : R_TRIG;
  rt_autoStart : R_TRIG;
  rt_mixComplete : R_TRIG;

  autoValveA/B... : BOOL; // maybe temp
END_VAR

Need define AUTO_STATE before function block. But maybe avoid DUT? Could use INT constants. Simpler use INT internal with constants to avoid nested DUT issue? We can define enum before block. User instructions say necessary named TYPE definitions may precede block. Good.

Need engineering contract comment with PUB IDs. But must include in same block before implementation. We need write up to 12 lines. Then CONTRACT_RULES JSON comment. Then TYPE and FB.

Need think about explicit output latching. CONTRACT_RULES for unconditional public Boolean output latch explicitly required by task. Manual outputs toggle and hold until next press? The outputs themselves are not unconditional latches necessarily because stop/estop/mode override. But maybe the manual state toggles hold until another rising edge or estop. The task says pressing button causes run, pressing again stops. That's a toggle latch. The public output hold is conditional on mode/estop. "unconditional public Boolean output latch explicitly required by task" maybe valveD in auto after process ends? It opens and process ends likely holds valveD? No reset input. But auto start resets it. Not unconditional. Manual outputs toggle, reset by same input rising edge, also estop. Not "hold_until_reset" with separate reset. So likely CONTRACT_RULES []. But need evaluate if any output should be declared hold_until_reset. For valveD after process ends maybe true until autoStart (reset) or estop. Could be hold_until_reset with reset_input=autoStart? But autoStart is edge not level. Not supported. Manual toggles: set_input and reset_input same button trigger; no separate public reset input, and estop override. So no unconditional latch. Use [].

Need implement. Let's design detailed auto state transitions with levels.

Enum:
TYPE AUTO_STATE : (IDLE, OPEN_A, OPEN_B, WAIT_C, MIXING, DONE);
END_TYPE

Inputs: estop, opeMode etc.

State variables and output temp.

In code:
// call R_TRIGs
rt_valveA(CLK := valveAStart);
...
rt_autoStart(CLK := autoStart);
rt_mixComplete(CLK := mixMotorComplete);

// emergency stop internal reset
IF NOT estop THEN
  manualValveA := FALSE; ... manualMixMotor := FALSE;
  autoState := AUTO_STATE#IDLE;
END_IF

// Manual toggles only if estop true and manual mode
IF estop AND NOT opeMode THEN
  IF rt_valveA.Q THEN manualValveA := NOT manualValveA; END_IF
  ...
END_IF

// Auto start
IF estop AND opeMode AND rt_autoStart.Q THEN
  autoState := AUTO_STATE#OPEN_A;
END_IF

Question: Should manual toggles be processed only in manual mode. Yes. If mode changed, manual states remain but no edges. okay.

// Auto state machine transitions only if estop and opeMode? We can encapsulate IF estop AND opeMode THEN transitions. But autoState may be forced IDLE if estop low. If estop true and opeMode true, process. Need avoid transitions when autoState IDLE? Use CASE.

IF estop AND opeMode THEN
  CASE autoState OF
    AUTO_STATE#OPEN_A:
      IF levelSensor >= 50 THEN
         autoState := AUTO_STATE#OPEN_B;
      END_IF
    AUTO_STATE#OPEN_B:
      IF levelSensor >= 80 THEN
         IF NOT processMode THEN
            autoState := AUTO_STATE#MIXING;
         ELSE
            autoState := AUTO_STATE#WAIT_C;
         END_IF
      END_IF
    AUTO_STATE#WAIT_C:
      IF levelSensor >= 100 THEN
         autoState := AUTO_STATE#MIXING;
      END_IF
    AUTO_STATE#MIXING:
      IF rt_mixComplete.Q THEN
         autoState := AUTO_STATE#DONE;
      END_IF
    AUTO_STATE#DONE:
      // stay until autoStart
  END_CASE
END_IF

Need consider autoStart edge may occur while state OPEN_A etc; resets to OPEN_A. We process autoStart before transitions? In code, if autoStart Q then state := OPEN_A; then transitions maybe same scan? If level >=50 same scan, could transition to OPEN_B immediately. But after autoStart, first opening A; if level already >=50, maybe close A open B same scan. Is that acceptable? Possibly okay because condition reached. But maybe should sequence at least one scan. Not specified. Usually press start, open A; next scan if sensor already at 50 then transition. If we process start then transitions same scan, it might skip A if level high. Not critical but could be seen as not opening A. The requirement "first opening valve A. When level reaches 50, close A..." On rising edge of autoStart, if level already at 50, the process should probably close A immediately? It says first opening A; maybe opening A for one scan. To be safe, separate state transitions from autoStart. We can set state to OPEN_A after transition computation, or use flag to block transition first scan. Simpler: order transitions first, then autoStart assignment. But if autoStart occurs while state DONE, transitions no issue; then set OPEN_A at end. That ensures autoStart output is OPEN_A that scan but state transitions not evaluated until next scan. Good. Manual edge logic separate.

So code ordering:
- R_TRIG update
- estop reset internal states
- manual toggles
- Auto state transitions IF estop AND opeMode THEN CASE old state...
- THEN handle autoStart: IF estop AND opeMode AND rt_autoStart.Q THEN autoState := OPEN_A; END_IF
But if autoStart edge and old state in MIXING, transitions might first complete due mixComplete same scan, then autoStart resets. Fine. If autoStart edge and old state OPEN_A with level >=50, would transition to OPEN_B then autoStart resets OPEN_A. Good. So start wins.

What if autoStart is pressed while auto mode and estop true but process not started (IDLE)? autoState set OPEN_A. Good.

Need compute auto outputs after transition/start. So:
local_autoValveA := FALSE; etc
CASE autoState OF
  AUTO_STATE#OPEN_A: local_autoValveA := TRUE;
  AUTO_STATE#OPEN_B: local_autoValveB := TRUE;
  AUTO_STATE#WAIT_C: local_autoValveC := TRUE;
  AUTO_STATE#MIXING: local_autoMixMotor := TRUE;
  AUTO_STATE#DONE: local_autoValveD := TRUE;
END_CASE
IDLE no outputs.

Then output assignments:
IF NOT estop THEN all false
ELSIF NOT opeMode THEN manual outputs
ELSE auto outputs
END_IF

Need consider mode switch from auto to manual. Auto state remains. If back to auto, auto process may continue from previous state without pressing autoStart. Is that acceptable? Requirements don't specify mode switch behavior. Could be unsafe. Maybe when operation mode changes, automatic process should not automatically resume. It says automatic mode operates according to process; manual mode manually. When switching to manual and back, likely auto process should stay where it was or reset? Not specified. But "equipment operates automatically according to process flow" in auto. If mode temporarily manual and back, maybe continue? Not specified. We can leave state. But if manual mode overrides outputs, auto state persists; on return to auto, process resumes. Maybe acceptable? Could also reset auto state on entering manual? But no requirement. Need mark unspecified. Maybe better to keep auto state as is; no invented resets. But emergency resets.

Manual states: When estop low, manualValveX false. If mode auto and back manual, manual states false. Good.

Need handle processMode sampled? Used at transition OPEN_B level >=80. What if processMode changes mid-process? Requirement says based on processMode. Could sample at start or when reaches 80. Probably at time condition. Use current input at transition. Fine.

Need handle mixMotorComplete in IDLE or other states. rt_mixComplete edge will be true even if not mixing; but transitions only case MIXING if Q. If autoStart and complete same scan, start wins? We transition before start assignment. If old state DONE then no transition, start assignment. If old state MIXING and complete and autoStart same scan, transition to DONE then start to OPEN_A. Good.

Potential issue R_TRIG instances called every scan even when estop false; okay.

Need check output latching with manual. Button edge toggles internal state; output equals state. If button held, no repeated toggles due R_TRIG. Great.

Need maybe include input `estop` description: FALSE emergency triggered, TRUE no emergency. We treat estop as TRUE safe.

Need exact interface names. Function block name can be e.g. MaterialProportioningControl. No specified name. Use `MaterialProportioningProcessControl`. Fine.

Need include TYPE before FB. Need no semicolon between END_STRUCT and END_TYPE if struct? We use enum no struct. Enum syntax:

END_TYPE
This is okay. Need maybe named type before FB. Fine.

Engineering contract comment within block: Should be inside ST comment before TYPE. They asked "Before implementing, put a concise ENGINEERING_CONTRACT comment inside the ST block (up to 12 lines). For each output or state group state: activation, retention/hold, explicit reset/deactivation, same-scan priority, and units/boundaries. Cite PUB clause IDs where relevant." Need do that. (* ENGINEERING_CONTRACT
 - Outputs valveARun..mixMotorRun:

Same-scan: autoStart wins over auto transitions; estop wins over all; manual edge evaluated only in manual/estop TRUE.

*)
